tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Review...', 'Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (agent won't start, gateway/action group fails, returns nothing, behaves differently in prod, which version is live), explicitly lists trigger contexts including ones the user may not name directly (runtime roles, VPC endpoints, SCPs, OTLP telemetry, aliasing), and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an agent will not start or cannot be invoked, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing or produces no traces, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific facts (AgentCore vs Classic distinctions, check-ids, API namespaces) without explaining generic AWS or LLM concepts. It assumes familiarity with AWS services and focuses on non-obvious operational specifics.
tests.evidence: "Bedrock AgentCore is where new work goes. Bedrock Agents Classic is in maintenance mode: per the AWS product-page End of Support Notice it is 'no longer available to new customers'..."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed catalogs (check-ids, thresholds, API field lists) are kept in references/ files and only summarized or pointed to in the body; the body itself does not embed large reference tables or detailed decision-tree data inline.
tests.evidence: "Every finding is grounded in the catalogs under references/: checks-agentcore.md (LLM-AC-001..010...) and checks-agents.md (LLM-AGT-001..011...)"

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked via markdown links in the body (Router table and Appendix section).
tests.evidence: "`references/checks-agents.md` — LLM-AGT-001..010 Bedrock Agents / action-group checks (primary)" appears alongside markdown links like `[LLM-AC-001)](references/checks-agentcore.md)` style entries in the Router table and Appendix.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The Router table ties each reference load to a specific trigger condition ('operator says X -> load Y'), clearly specifying when to load each file.
tests.evidence: "AgentCore runtime will not start / cannot invoke | `ListAgentRuntimes` / `GetAgentRuntime` for status, version, role ARN | `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001)"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.
tests.evidence: "`references/checks-agentcore.md`" and similar relative paths used throughout.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (permission checks, alias resolution, read-only API sequence) are given exact ordered steps, while flexible areas (which checks to prioritize, how to word findings) are described with rationale rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: "The permission checks depend on reading the runtime first, so do not skip ahead." paired with flexible guidance like "If it is unclear, resolve which service is in play before collecting — do not run both catalogs blindly."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple migration paths or APIs could be used, the skill designates a primary default while mentioning alternatives explicitly, e.g., migration paths are presented with the harness as closest analog.
tests.evidence: "recommend migrating via the AgentCore harness (config-based, closest analog) or code-defined agents on AgentCore"

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedures teach a generalizable method (resolve alias before concluding, simulate IAM policy, check gateway targets) applicable to any workload, not a one-off instance-specific declaration.
tests.evidence: "Step 2: Resolve each alias with `ListAgentAliases` / `GetAgentAlias` to the version it serves; treat that version — not the latest prepared DRAFT — as production behaviour (LLM-AGT-007)."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section documenting concrete, specific pitfalls (alias vs DRAFT, AccessDenied misinterpretation, no-datapoints vs zero, deprecated namespace) that defy naive assumptions.
tests.evidence: "'The AgentCore read returned AccessDenied, so no runtime exists.' The standard `AIDevOpsAgentAccessPolicy` does not include the `bedrock-agentcore` namespace..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured review reports and provides a dedicated template asset referenced for assembling output.
tests.evidence: "assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md — consolidated review output (scope, findings with check-ids and severities, remediation, disclosed gaps)"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the report template is kept in assets/ and referenced, with only a severity table (short) inline.
tests.evidence: The body contains only a short Severity Definitions table, not a full report skeleton; the actual template is in "assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md".

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced multiple times in the body (procedures and appendix).
tests.evidence: "assemble per the report template." and "the output follows `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md`."

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies the condition under which to load it (when a full report is requested).
tests.evidence: "When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md`."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: Both procedures (AgentCore and Classic review) are presented as ordered checkbox checklists with 'Step N:' labeling, satisfying the required format.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its own findings for evidence, masking, and completeness before presenting.
tests.evidence: "Before you present an agent/runtime review, re-check your own output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
